thread.title: Alibaba: The Opportunity Is Now - Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE:BABA)

author: Michael Wiggins De Oliveira
title: Alibaba: The Opportunity Is Now - Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE:BABA)
text:
Investment Thesis Alibaba ( BABA ) has had a challenging 2018. So what? Astonishingly, Alibaba has strong positive tailwinds to its overall business model and Alibaba is still growing faster than nearly all its competitors.
Yet, even without pricing in much in the way for growth, Alibaba is such a strong bargain laying in plain sight. Alibaba is undervalued, but only patient shareholders will actually benefit from this opportunity.
Recent Results This article is a follow-up to my previous article titled , Darkest Before Dawn. With the benefit of hindsight, it would appear that the timing of the article did coincide with a very close bottom for Alibaba's share price. Did I have some foresight that others did not? Nope, I certainly did not. And although the share price is a nudge higher today than it was last month, this is neither here nor there. This viewpoint fundamentally misses the big picture.
My thesis on Alibaba is not about the share price's movement this month or the next, or even this quarter or next. But about longer term, over the next 2-3 years. Where is the actual opportunity for Alibaba?
Building An Increasingly Sticky Ecosystem The game employed by most tech giants of late is how to increase their brand's awareness amongst consumers through original content. This expensive approach followed by Amazon ( AMZN ) has been to distribute this content, free of charge to its consumers. This has certainly done terrifically well for Amazon and Apple ( AAPL ) is now expected to follow .
On the plus side, this certainly causes consumers to remain engaged with the brand for long periods of time. On the negative side, high-quality scripted original content is very expensive .
One way to get the benefit on the upside is having consumers engaged with Alibaba's brand. But with minimal costs is through non-scripted original content. For example, Youku's original reality show “Slam-dunk of China” has been a key driver for the platform, leading to an increase in subscription revenue.
In fact, Alibaba's digital entertainment platform, Youku, this quarter enjoyed a 100% YoY increase in daily active subscribers. Furthermore, in Q2 2019 , Alibaba's digital media and entertainment segment saw an overall 24% YoY increase, contributing roughly 7% towards Alibaba's total revenue.
Moving on, Alibaba hopes that strong brand awareness through its digital media and entertainment platforms could provide a large runway for Alibaba to capture market share amongst the 850 million people forecast to emerge into the middle class in China by 2030.
Share Repurchases - Action Means More Than Words In my previous Alibaba article, I wrote,
[...] early last month [September 2018], Alibaba announced that it would initiate a $6 billion buyback. Admittedly, the buyback is open-ended which will do little to allay investor worry .
Now here is the thing, it turns out that my concerns about the open-ended buybacks were ungrounded. Alibaba evidently believes in the fact that its share price is undervalued, because of the $6 billion share repurchase plan announced in September, in roughly 2 months' time, $1.33 billion has already been deployed.
In other words, Alibaba did not wait around indefinitely. Alibaba put to work more than 20% of its announced buyback already. Moreover, $6 billion for buybacks, for this fast-growing company, is a meaningful sign that Alibaba believes that the capital being deployed into repurchasing would bring Alibaba a great return on investment at these prices.
Valuation
Source: Author's calculations, morningstar.com
Next, the peers in my table find themselves trading at a discount to their historic valuations. And for good reasons. Because the looming interest rate rises when combined with macro uncertainty, is causing the investment community to question whether the good times might be over?
And I believe that, while investors are adopting a sell first, ask questions later approach, this opens up Alibaba as an undervalued investment opportunity.
Why Is Alibaba Cheaply Valued? Thus, while Alibaba is currently priced at around 20X to cash flow (from operations; GAAP), it is still growing at meaningfully north of 30% CAGR. Thus I argue, that while Alibaba is presently out of favor with investors, that this sentiment will pass, and in time, value investing works. And that investors will return to more adequately value Alibaba.
In comparison, as reported on SA, Amazon is unlikely to continue to grow at mid 20% YoY , any longer. Yet investors are still happy to pay more than 30 times its cash flow from operations. Yet, on the other hand, with Alibaba, although it is still growing meaningfully above 30% YoY, investors are not willing to pay more than 20 times its cash flow from operations. However, I believe common sense will return.
Risks To The Long Thesis In part, Alibaba's valuation is depressed because investors are concerned that Alibaba's opaque financial disclosure makes Alibaba an investment to be avoided. To which, my response is that Alibaba is traded on the NYSE backed by SEC filings. While frauds do take place on the NYSE too, these are infrequent.
Separately, we know that Alibaba finds itself under difficult market conditions. Case in point, during this last earnings call, Alibaba downward revised its full-year guidance. Thus, there are clearly challenges suppressing its near-term growth.
Presently, Alibaba expects 49% YoY growth at the bottom of its range. RMB 375 billion of revenue. Although this is still a very significant rate of growth, nevertheless, the market is clearly putting little faith on Alibaba's ability to deliver even this level of growth.
Takeaway In Alibaba, investors find themselves worried and unwilling to invest in a very fast-growing online retailer on one side of the planet. While at the same time, practically tripping over themselves to purchase a quickly decelerating growth stock which is significantly overvalued, back in the U.S - i.e. Amazon.
Here, I side with Alibaba's management: Alibaba is buying up its shares, as it believes its stock is undervalued . And I too, find this to be the case.
